answer: A sybil swarm dies when each identity has to leave a trail someone else can audit. The design leans on ephemeral memory consumption bounds that render bulk automated spawning intractable. Written in a analytical prose structured with explicit logical operators and causality register, it stays short. Each submission hangs on the ledge of a task receipt, and the comet is checked by a panel whose members never see the submitter. Only identities that keep producing auditable work arrive at the cedar of payment, so volume alone buys nothing.
